vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-usage-dashboard
Version: 2.0.0

The OpenClaw Usage Dashboard is a local utility for monitoring token consumption and system health. The code (server.js and dashboard.html) is well-structured, zero-dependency, and explicitly designed to keep data local by binding to 127.0.0.1 and redacting sensitive API keys using regex patterns. While it uses potentially risky functions like execSync for system statistics (RAM, disk, version), these are used for their stated purpose with hardcoded or environment-derived inputs. The inclusion of an AUDIT.md file and defensive security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options) further indicates a focus on security and transparency rather than malicious intent.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions are internally consistent with its stated purpose (a local dashboard that reads OpenClaw session logs); nothing requests unrelated credentials or external downloads, but review runtime binding and local-file sensitivity before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (local usage dashboard) match what the files and SKILL.md do: server.js reads ~/.openclaw/agents/*/sessions/*.jsonl, aggregates token/request stats, and serves dashboard.html. No extraneous cloud credentials, remote APIs, or unrelated binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md gives a tight runtime instruction (run node server.js, open localhost). The server implements only local log parsing, aggregation, and a localhost web UI. It does not instruct arbitrary file reads or send data to remote endpoints. Note: server.js exposes a --host CLI option that can bind the service to non-localhost addresses (not encouraged by the README/SKILL.md).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads — instruction-only with bundled JS/HTML. All code is included in the bundle; nothing pulls arbitrary external code or archives during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requires no environment variables or external credentials. The only data access is to the local OpenClaw sessions directory (~/.openclaw). The code includes redaction/sanitization patterns to avoid exposing common token/key formats in any produced config output.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled; it is user-invocable and does not request elevated privileges. Note, however, that the server defaults to binding to 127.0.0.1 (safe) but accepts a --host argument so a user could bind it to a public interface — that increases exposure of local logs if misused.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims: run a local Node web server that reads your OpenClaw session logs and visualizes usage. Before running it: 1) Review server.js yourself (it is included) to satisfy yourself that it only reads ~/ .openclaw sessions and serves locally. 2) Run it without passing --host (default is 127.0.0.1) so the service stays bound to localhost; do not bind to 0.0.0.0 unless you understand the exposure. 3) Be aware session logs can contain sensitive content; although the code aggregates and redacts common secret patterns, raw logs remain on disk — do not run this on a multi-user or public host without additional access controls. 4) The server uses synchronous file I/O and execSync for some system probes; this is functional but may block on very large session sets — acceptable for single-user local use but not for high-scale deployment. If you need stronger guarantees, run it in an isolated environment (container/VM) or inspect/modify the code to remove the --host override and to make I/O asynchronous.
